subject: Decision framework for marketplace listing vs direct contract — approval timelines & PO controls
messages:

Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com

Subject: Marketplace vs direct PO — need guidance for legal & PO timing

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We're preparing procurement paperwork for the patient-data routing pilot and need help deciding whether to go through the cloud marketplace (GCP Marketplace preferred) or sign a direct contract / PO with Redwood. Key constraints from our side:

- Our legal team prefers the simplest route for audit trails and tax handling.
- Finance requires we lock the unit pricing into a PO by Aug 2 to meet our monthly close.
- Co-sell credits / partner discounts are baked into the budget request; we need to know timing so we can record forecasted partner revenue.

Can you outline the tradeoffs (timelines, invoice path, who is seller-of-record, impact on co-sell credits, and any procurement controls that differ)? I've attached a short RFP summary (helix_rfp_summary.pdf).

If a quick 20-min sync helps, we can open a slot tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Ruth

Helix Health

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Ruth Lin <ruth.lin@helixhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace vs direct PO — need guidance for legal & PO timing

Hi Ruth — thanks for the clear constraints and the RFP. TL;DR: both routes work, but they differ on timing and invoice mechanics. Below is a concise framework and recommended next steps.

Marketplace (GCP / AWS / Azure):
- Time to invoice: Fast once listing / private offer exists; public listing can add weeks for listing approvals depending on cloud provider. Private Offer via marketplace usually takes ~3–10 business days once we push the offer and your procurement accepts it.
- Seller of record: Often the marketplace partner (cloud marketplace) acts as reseller; Redwood will still be the underlying vendor for co-sell attribution in partner systems.
- Co-sell credits: For partner-led deals, co-sell credits are typically recognized after the private offer is accepted and invoice is processed; there can be a delay of 1–2 billing cycles for revenue recognition in cloud marketplace reporting.
- PO controls: You get a marketplace invoice rather than a Redwood invoice; PO number acceptance is supported in private offers and acceptance screens, but some finance teams prefer direct Redwood POs for reconciliation.
- Tax / resale: Marketplace invoices may reflect marketplace tax treatment (varies by provider/region).

Direct contract / Direct PO:
- Time to invoice: We can issue a Redwood invoice as soon as contracts are signed and PO is received — typically the most predictable path for tight close timelines.
- Seller of record: Redwood. Easier for tax and reseller scenarios.
- Co-sell credits: Can be applied immediately in our partner reporting once the contract is executed; no marketplace lag.
- PO controls: Direct PO maps cleanly to your internal systems and is usually preferred for strict PO acceptance policies.

Recommendation based on your timeline (need PO by Aug 2):
- If you need an invoice/PO locked by Aug 2, the safest route is a direct PO + short form MSA amendment now. That ensures a Redwood invoice and no marketplace listing dependency.
- If you prefer marketplace for procurement policy or vendor consolidation, we can create a private offer today and your finance team can accept it — but we should confirm acceptance flows and allow for the 3–10 business day window.

Attachments: attaching our latest pricing matrix for quick reference (pricing-sheet-v2.pdf).

Next steps:
- If direct PO: please share your PO template and signer details; we can produce a draft invoice today.
- If marketplace private offer: we'll prepare a private offer and share the acceptance link (DocuSign/private-offer) — we need an OK from your procurement to accept in the cloud console.

Would you like to hop on a 20-min call at 2pm PT today? I can include Marissa to walk through partner credit timing.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Ruth — quick add from pricing & partner side:

- Co-sell credit mechanics: If we go direct, we can immediately tag the deal in our partner portal and apply the negotiated co-sell percentage to ARR at close. In marketplace private-offer flows, the credit is applied after the cloud provider confirms the invoice, which can add 30–60 days before the cloud partner reports it back to us.
- Discounting: We can mirror the private-offer pricing in a direct PO (identical SKUs) so you get the same economics either way.
- Expediting listings: For GCP, Marketplace listing approvals can be expedited but require our product compliance checklist and a short security attestation — we can prioritize if you prefer that route.

If you need the PO template, Hannah (cc'd) can help with the legal language and signature routing. For timing-sensitive closes, direct PO + Redwood invoice avoids any marketplace reporting lag.

Link: HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654

Marissa Cole

We'll prepare the signed PO and aim to transmit by EOD tomorrow. If you can send a one-line confirmation of terms and the Redwood billing contact for remittance, we'll finalize internally.
